about.en:
The UCL Global Undergraduate Scholarship helps international students from low-income backgrounds take a full-time bachelor's degree at University College London, one of the world's top-10 universities. In the latest round UCL offered up to 33 awards: 10 covering full tuition fees plus a maintenance allowance and a fixed allowance for extras such as the visa and Immigration Health Surcharge, 20 covering full tuition only, and 3 full-tuition awards reserved for students from India.

Selection is purely on financial need. UCL treats a household income of about £42,875 or less as 'low income', but it still considers applicants above that figure. Shortlisted candidates send financial evidence in mid-May and results come out in early June, before the UCAS reply deadline. The award runs for the standard length of the degree.

It is one of very few UK scholarships that can cover the whole cost of a degree for an international student, so if your family cannot pay London fees it is worth applying the moment UCL confirms your fee status.

about.en:
Reach Oxford Scholarships (formerly Oxford Student Scholarships) are for students from countries that receive official development assistance who, for political or financial reasons or because suitable education does not exist, cannot study for a degree at home. The list of eligible nationalities is long and includes, among others, Georgia, Türkiye, Egypt, Jordan, Morocco, India, Pakistan, Nigeria, Kenya, Ukraine and Brazil.

The award pays course fees, a grant for living costs and one return air fare each year for the full 3–4 years of the degree. It can be held in any subject except Medicine, at any college. Selection looks at the highest academic ability, financial need, social commitment and the intention to return home after graduating. Only around 2–3 scholarships are given each year, so it is extremely competitive.

For 2027 entry the scholarship application window opens in January 2027 and closes on 26 January 2027; you can only apply if you already applied to Oxford by 15 October 2026 and received an offer. Students who missed that UCAS deadline should plan for 2028 entry.

about.en:
The Cambridge Trust is the University of Cambridge's main funder of international students. Its Global Impact Scholarship is aimed at undergraduate applicants with overseas fee status and a high level of financial need who have overcome significant challenges to win a place at Cambridge. It can be held at any College and in any subject.

The value is a full package: the international University tuition fee, the College fee, annual maintenance sufficient for a single student, the student visa and the Immigration Health Surcharge. There is no separate scholarship application before admission: once a College makes you an offer, it sends you the Cambridge Trust application and you are considered for every Trust award you qualify for. Most awards are made in February and March.

For 2027 entry, the UCAS deadline for Cambridge was 15 October 2026, so this record is relevant for students who applied in that round (and for anyone planning 2028 entry). Cambridge's general undergraduate funding for internationals is limited, which makes this one of the few routes to a fully funded Cambridge degree.

about.en:
Imperial Inspires is Imperial College London's large new scholarship programme for international students. For autumn 2027 entry Imperial is offering at least 300 awards of £15,000 per year, for each year of the course, across its four faculties: Engineering, Natural Sciences, Medicine and the Business School. It covers undergraduate degrees including integrated master's courses (MEng, MSci).

The scholarship is merit-based: Imperial looks for academic excellence, curiosity, initiative, leadership and a global outlook, and region of origin is not a factor. After you apply through UCAS, eligible applicants who meet the course's minimum entry requirements are invited (from October 2026) to answer an additional optional essay question, which is the scholarship application. Awards are made by mid-April 2027 and cannot be deferred.

£15,000 does not cover the full overseas fee (about £40,000+ a year), but over a four-year MEng it is worth £60,000 and can sometimes be combined with other awards.

about.en:
The LSE Undergraduate Support Scheme (USS) is the London School of Economics' main financial aid for international undergraduates. It is for students with overseas fee status, holding an offer for any LSE bachelor's programme, who do not have the funds to cover all their costs of study.

Awards are tailored to each student's circumstances and are usually between £15,000 and £25,000 per year, renewed for each year of the programme subject to satisfactory progress. LSE receives far more applications than it can fund, so not every applicant succeeds. LSE also runs donor-funded scholarships (for example the Uggla Family Scholars Programme) that can be combined with USS.

LSE is one of the world's leading social-science universities (economics, international relations, politics, law, finance). The scheme makes it realistic for strong students from middle-income families to attend.

about.en:
The Edinburgh Global Undergraduate Mathematics Scholarships are awarded by the University of Edinburgh to international applicants with outstanding academic results who are accepted for full-time undergraduate study in the School of Mathematics (degrees in mathematics, statistics and their joint programmes).

Each scholarship is worth £5,000, paid in instalments towards living costs, and continues for the length of the programme as long as you make satisfactory progress. Several awards are made each year. You must have applied via UCAS, but you can complete the scholarship application before receiving an offer.

Edinburgh's School of Mathematics is one of the strongest in the UK, and Scottish four-year degrees give a broad first year. The award is modest compared with overseas fees, but it is renewable and relatively accessible for strong maths students.

about.en:
The University of St Andrews, Scotland's oldest university and consistently near the top of UK league tables, offers International Undergraduate Scholarships to students with overseas fee status beginning an undergraduate degree in 2027. The award is a tuition-fee reduction applied every year of the degree.

It is assessed on financial need. Applicants are encouraged to describe circumstances such as a case for financial need, previous needs-based funding, a disadvantaged neighbourhood, a disability or belonging to a minority group. You enter your gross annual household income in GBP. The course and funding applications are independent, so applying does not affect your admission decision. A separate Accommodation Award (£1,900 a year) shares the same deadline.

The exact value will be confirmed by December 2026. It is available in almost every School (from Computer Science and International Relations to Medicine), but not for the joint BA International Honours with William & Mary, which has its own scholarship.

about.en:
Durham University's Inspiring Excellence Undergraduate Scholarship is a competitive, merit-based partial award for international applicants. It comes in two sizes: £5,000 per year (up to £15,000 over a three-year degree) or £10,000 per year (up to £30,000), applied as a discount on tuition for programmes starting in September 2027.

Selection considers your scholarship answers, academic achievement and potential to make a positive impact, while also balancing nationalities and programmes. You do not need an offer to apply, only a UCAS ID. If you are not selected in round 1, you are automatically reconsidered in round 2. Successful students must make Durham their Firm Choice by the UCAS reply deadline.

Durham is a collegiate top-10 UK university known for law, economics, natural sciences, history and engineering. Note the restrictions: the award cannot be combined with any other scholarship or sponsorship, and it excludes Clearing, the International Study Centre route and two theology degrees.

You must be classed as an overseas student for fees and have applied, or be about to apply, for an eligible in-person undergraduate course. You do not need an offer before applying. The single online form also puts you forward for other awards you qualify for, such as GREAT Scholarships and some donor bursaries. Outcomes are sent by the end of May 2027.

Bristol is a Russell Group university ranked in the global top 60, strong in engineering, computer science, economics, law and the life sciences.

The University of Glasgow's World Changers Global Excellence Scholarship rewards international and EU (non-UK) undergraduates with excellent grades. For 2027 entry it is a tuition-fee discount of £10,000 a year in the Colleges of Medical, Veterinary & Life Sciences and Science & Engineering, and £7,000 a year in Arts and Social Sciences, renewed annually with satisfactory progress.

There is no application form: everyone who receives an offer is automatically assessed against published grade thresholds (achieved or predicted), for example AAB / IB 36 for most sciences and humanities, AAA / IB 38 for psychology and the Adam Smith Business School, and A*AA / IB 39 for law, computing science and James Watt MEng. Medicine, Dentistry and Veterinary Medicine are excluded. Candidates under consideration hear within two weeks of their offer.

Glasgow is a Russell Group university in the world top 80, and Scottish four-year degrees give flexibility in the first two years.

The Global Futures Scholarship is the University of Manchester's main merit award for international students from selected countries. For September 2027 entry it funds more than 350 partial scholarships worth over £6 million in total, across undergraduate and master's courses.

It is open to residents of 23 countries: Bangladesh, Botswana, Canada, Egypt, Ghana, India, Indonesia, Kenya, Malaysia, Mauritius, Nigeria, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Singapore, South Africa, Sri Lanka, Taiwan (master's only), Thailand, Türkiye, the United Arab Emirates, the United States, Vietnam and Zimbabwe. Award levels, criteria and deadlines differ for each country and are listed on the university's country profile pages.

You must already hold an offer for a full-time, on-campus Manchester course starting in September 2027; the university then emails eligible offer-holders an online application form. Manchester is a large Russell Group university ranked in the global top 40.

about.en:
Bocconi University in Milan, one of Europe's leading schools for economics, finance, management, law and data science, funds first-year bachelor's students through one application called Bocconi4Access to Education. For 2027-28 first-year tuition is €17,700, and the scheme can reduce it by 20% to 100%: full (100%) waivers and 80%/60% partial waivers under Bocconi4Access, and 40%/20% waivers under the Boost your Future scholarship for students who still need significant help.

Awards are based on the economic and asset situation of your family household, assessed by Bocconi's Fees, Funding and Housing Office, and are allocated until the budget runs out, so applying in an early session matters. Waivers renew for the legal duration of the course if you meet merit requirements. Separate non-means-tested waivers exist (Women award, siblings, sport, disability), and from year two the best students can win full-tuition Excellence awards.

about.en:
The University of Padua, founded in 1222 and one of Italy's top research universities, awards up to 76 Padua International Excellence Scholarships across its English-taught bachelor's and master's degrees. Each scholarship pays €8,000 gross per academic year (two instalments of €4,000) and waives university tuition, so winners pay only the regional tax and a revenue stamp. Bachelor's and single-cycle students can hold it for up to three years.

There is no separate form: applying to an eligible English-taught degree before the admission deadline automatically enters you, and each degree's Teaching Committee selects winners on academic excellence and prior record, mainly in the first call. To keep the award you must earn at least 20 ECTS credits by 30 November of the following year. Padua also offers 100 separate full fee waivers for international students in English-taught degrees.

about.en:
In Italy, regional 'right to study' (DSU) agencies give means-tested scholarships to students at public universities, and international students are eligible on the same basis as Italians. DiSCo Lazio serves universities in Rome and the Lazio region, including Sapienza, Tor Vergata and Roma Tre. Winners typically receive a cash scholarship (larger for students living away from home), exemption from university tuition, and access to subsidised housing and canteens.

Eligibility depends on family income and assets, calculated for foreign families through an 'ISEE parificato' using documents from your home country (income, property, family composition), translated and legalised. First-year awards are confirmed once you earn the required credits. The call is strict and non-extendable, so start collecting documents as soon as you apply to your university.

about.en:
ER.GO is the regional right-to-study agency for Emilia-Romagna, home to the University of Bologna (the world's oldest university) and the universities of Modena and Reggio Emilia, Parma and Ferrara. In 2025/26 it invested over €160 million in scholarships and services. Winners receive a cash scholarship whose amount depends on family income and on whether they are resident, commuter or off-site students, plus a full exemption from university tuition, a refund of the regional tax, and the option to convert part of the grant into meal vouchers; off-site students can also apply for ER.GO housing.

International students qualify under the same economic and merit rules, with family income certified from home-country documents. ER.GO runs a dedicated International Students section with step-by-step guides, including how to get an Italian tax code.

Covers Bologna, Modena-Reggio, Parma and Ferrara universities

about.en:
IE University (Madrid and Segovia) is a private, highly international university known for business, international relations, law, architecture, computer science and data. Its undergraduate IE Awards are open to every nationality and programme and cover between 10% and 60% of tuition. They are assessed on both merit and financial need, so families must submit a financial questionnaire. Named awards include the IE Academic Achievement Award (for averages around 9/10, 3.8/4 GPA, IB 38/45 or equivalent), Personal Excellence (extracurriculars), Young Entrepreneurs, Women in STEM, Sustainability, Humanities and Collaboration awards. IE Foundation partner scholarships are listed separately and may require an extra essay.

Check coverage carefully: IE's standard awards are partial (up to 60% of tuition, which is about €20,000+ per year). Higher coverage comes only through specific partner or foundation scholarships. You can select up to three awards but receive only one, and awards renew each year if you meet renewal criteria.

about.en:
Esade, one of Europe's top business and law schools, runs a €5 million Scholarship Program; about 8.4% of its undergraduates hold a scholarship, with an average 84% of tuition covered. Degree Talent Scholarships (Dedicated, Future and Class Talent Scholarships, named after their donors) cover between 60% and 100% of tuition for the entire BBA, Law, BITLASI or double-degree programme, based on academic results and financial need. Complements include Esade Lodging Grants for students who live outside Barcelona province and Esade Living Grants for transport and general expenses.

To qualify you need an average of 8.5/10 in the last two years of school or an equivalent: IB 33/42, French Bac 16.2/20, or 85% of the maximum in other systems, and SAT 1300+ if you submit the SAT. Family income must not exceed €118,000 gross a year for a family of four, with assets also assessed.

Separate from its need-based Talent Scholarships, Esade offers Academic Merit Awards for bachelor's applicants with excellent records. They are renewable and can cover up to 100% of tuition. The programme includes the Best University Access Grade Award and the Academic Excellence and Distinction Awards, each with its own requirements.

You must already be admitted to your degree or double degree, then apply in the Candidate Portal following the award guide. The committee looks at your academic record at admission plus award-specific documents. You may apply for only one award; once granted it is not reviewed again, and it can be combined with a Talent Scholarship or Esade's Income-Share Agreement as long as the total does not exceed 100% of tuition.

about.en:
The University of Navarra (Pamplona, with campuses in Madrid, San Sebastián and Barcelona) is a leading private Spanish university, highly ranked for medicine, communication, law, business and architecture. Its main undergraduate scholarship, the Beca Alumni, supports students with an excellent secondary-school record who face financial difficulties. The amount is personalised: the committee looks at tuition, housing costs, other scholarships and how much the family can contribute.

A newer University of Navarra Aid Programme gives personalised aid to students with good grades and demonstrated need. International students with top-5% class rank can also get a 16% first-year honours discount, and faculties offer their own awards (e.g. Prof. Jiménez Vargas Scholarship in Medicine). For 2027/28, admissions opened on 1 October 2026, with main rounds on 9 December 2026 and 9 March 2027.

about.en:
Koç University in Istanbul is Türkiye's top-ranked private research university, teaching in English across business, economics, engineering, law, social sciences and natural sciences. Every admitted international undergraduate is evaluated by the Admissions Committee for a merit scholarship on academic merit only (need-blind), covering 25%, 50%, 75% or 100% of annual tuition for the duration of the programme.

There is no separate scholarship application: results arrive with your admission offer. Strong standardised scores (SAT/ACT, IB, A-levels or equivalents) are essential, as applying without one significantly lowers both admission and scholarship chances. Merit scholarships cover tuition only (no housing or living costs), and the School of Medicine offers no scholarships to internationals. Country-specific programmes (e.g. Azerbaijan State Scholarship, HEC Pakistan, Türkiye Burslari at Koç) are listed separately.

about.en:
Aalto University in Espoo (Helsinki region) is Finland's leading university for technology, business, and art and design. Non-EU/EEA students in its English-taught bachelor's programmes pay €12,000 a year (technology, business, multidisciplinary) or €15,000 (art and architecture). Students of all nationalities at public and state-recognised universities can apply, including those just starting their first semester. In 2022 around 30,500 students received it.

Selection is by each university and looks at grades and academic potential, social commitment and personal achievements such as overcoming obstacles in your background. Your income and that of your parents play no role. Many sponsors add mentoring, networking or internships. Because most German public universities charge little or no tuition, €300 a month makes a real contribution to living costs. Apply through the university where you enrol, by its own deadline.

about.en:
Bilkent University in Ankara was Türkiye's first private, non-profit university and is known for engineering, computer science, economics, business, and music and performing arts, all taught in English. International applicants who want financial support are assessed on their high-school grades, national or international exam scores (e.g. SAT, IB, A-levels), programme choice and other academic criteria.

Tuition waivers are awarded at five levels from 20% to 100% in 20% steps, and a limited number of top students holding a full waiver may also receive accommodation. Scholarships last up to 10 semesters for four-year degrees provided you take the minimum course load and keep an annual GPA of at least 2.00 (2.50 for accommodation). Later, top-5% students can earn merit waivers. Applicants who hold or have held Turkish citizenship are not eligible.

en: Tuition waivers of 20%–100%
Possible dorm place for top full-waiver students
Assessed automatically from your application

eligibility.en: International applicants (never Turkish citizens) applying to a Bilkent undergraduate programme, with strong high-school grades and accepted exam scores.

en: Prepare transcripts, exam scores (SAT/ACT, IB, A-levels or national exams) and English proficiency
Apply through Bilkent's online international application form during the 2027 window
Indicate you are seeking financial assistance
Receive the scholarship level with your admission decision

costs.en: Waiver covers 20–100% of tuition (Bilkent international tuition is roughly US$15,000–$20,000 a year). Living costs in Ankara are relatively low.

score_reason: Up to 100% tuition plus possible housing; 2027 dates estimated.

coverage_note.en: Tuition waiver at 20/40/60/80/100%; accommodation for a limited number of full-waiver holders.

about.en:
Sabancı University in Istanbul is a research-intensive English-medium private university known for its interdisciplinary first year and strengths in engineering, computer science, economics and management. International applicants who meet the requirements are automatically considered for admission scholarships, and the scholarship section of the application is optional.

The Scholarship Committee weighs academic background, reference letters, exam results, transcripts, interview results and evidence of achievements such as competition prizes or olympiad certificates. Scholarship numbers are limited at every level, early applicants get priority, and a set score does not guarantee a given level. Once awarded at admission, the scholarship continues for the regular length of the degree. Students can also request in-study scholarships after two strong semesters.

en: Automatic consideration for all international applicants
Holds for the whole degree once awarded
Early applicants get priority

eligibility.en: International applicants meeting Sabancı's undergraduate requirements (one accepted exam/diploma with a valid score, official transcript, language proficiency if required).

en: Create an account on the Sabancı application portal when the Fall 2027 cycle opens (expected December 2026)
Upload transcript, exam/diploma score, language score, references and achievements
Optionally complete the scholarship section
Attend an interview if invited; the scholarship decision comes with admission

costs.en: Scholarship levels (share of tuition) are not published. Sabancı tuition for international students is roughly US$20,000+ a year.

score_reason: Automatic consideration at a top Turkish university, but award levels are not published and dates are estimated.

coverage_note.en: Partial or full tuition scholarships; levels not published (estimate).

summary.ar: منح جدارة تلقائية من 3,000 إلى 21,500 فرنك سويسري سنوياً للطلاب الدوليين في جامعة فرانكلين، وهي جامعة فنون حرة على النمط الأمريكي في لوغانو، إضافة إلى جوائز خاصة تصل إلى 10,000 دولار. الموعد ذو الأولوية 1 ديسمبر.

about.en:
Franklin University Switzerland in Lugano is a small, US-accredited liberal-arts university offering English-taught bachelor's degrees in international relations, business, economics, environmental studies and more, with academic travel built into the curriculum. Merit awards are given automatically at admission based on recalculated GPA: for international students CHF 21,500 (GPA 3.80–4.00), CHF 17,500 (3.50–3.79), CHF 13,000 (3.00–3.49) or CHF 3,000 (below 3.00) per year, renewable for seven semesters. Students on the lower Swiss/EU/EEA tuition rate are not eligible.

Special awards can be added on top, such as the Franklin Honors Program Award ($3,000–$10,000, deadline 1 December), the Ambassador Wilfried Geens Award ($3,000, IB/AP students) and awards for sustainability and creative practice (deadlines 1 March). Note that international tuition is high (about CHF 52,750 plus fees), so even the top merit award covers well under half.

en: CHF 3,000–21,500 per year, automatic
Stackable special awards up to $10,000
Priority deadline 1 December 2026

eligibility.en: International (non-Swiss/EU-rate) first-year applicants to Franklin's bachelor's programmes; award tier set by recalculated high-school GPA.

en: Apply through Franklin's admissions portal (priority by 1 December 2026)
Merit award is calculated automatically from your transcript
For special awards, submit the extra statement/portfolio/interview by 1 December or 1 March
Receive the award with your admission letter

costs.en: International tuition about CHF 52,750 a year plus ~CHF 2,650 fees; merit award reduces this by CHF 3,000–21,500. Housing and Swiss health insurance are extra.

score_reason: Automatic and transparent, but high net cost even after the award.

coverage_note.en: CHF 3,000–21,500 per year (up to ~40% of CHF 52,750 tuition).

about.en:
Leiden University College The Hague (LUC) is Leiden University's selective, residential honours college offering the Liberal Arts and Sciences: Global Challenges bachelor's in English. For 2027-28 the non-EU/EEA tuition is €18,050 (€21,120 including the institutional fee). Because the Dutch NL Scholarship is not available at Leiden for 2026-27 and 2027-28, LUC's own Financial Support Programme is the main aid for incoming international students.

Awards are €1,000–€3,000 a year, normally for up to three years and reviewed annually. You need documentary evidence that you cannot study at LUC without support, and you must be (conditionally) admitted during the March–May selection period. Applicants upload a motivation letter, a financial plan on LUC's template and supporting documents in uSis.

en: €1,000–€3,000 per year for up to 3 years
All nationalities, based on financial need
Window expected 1 Dec 2026 – 15 Mar 2027

eligibility.en: Prospective LUC students of any nationality who have applied for admission, are (conditionally) admitted during selection, hold no prior bachelor's or master's degree, and can document financial need.

Upload a motivation letter, LUC financial-plan template and supporting documents
Submit before 15 March (expected); decisions around 21 April; accept within 2 weeks

coverage_note.en: €1,000–€3,000 per year (≈5–15% of non-EU tuition).

about.en:
The BA (International Honours) is a four-year joint degree between the University of St Andrews and William & Mary in the USA: students spend two years at each and choose Classics, Film Studies, Economics, English, History or International Relations. The Scholarship for Excellence is for gifted students entering the first year in 2027, selected purely on academic merit, and open to Scottish, rest-of-UK and overseas applicants with no geographical restriction.

Scholars represent the university at events and in publications. The value will be confirmed by early December 2026 and the award runs for four years. You can apply once you have submitted your course application (an offer is not needed). The application window closes on 17 March 2027 and the BA (International Honours) Common Application deadline is 1 May 2027.

Open to all nationalities
Closes 17 March 2027

about.en:
St Andrews' International Accommodation Award helps overseas-fee undergraduates with financial need meet housing costs in a small town where accommodation is a major expense. It is worth £1,900 a year for the duration of the course: paid towards University halls in the first instance, or as ten monthly maintenance payments (with a double payment in February) if you live privately.

You apply through the same International Undergraduate Scholarships form as the need-based tuition scholarship, two working days after submitting your course application, without waiting for an offer. Information is considered holistically and only used for scholarship assessment.

en: £1,900 per year for the whole course
Same form as the International Undergraduate Scholarship
Closes 27 January 2027

en: Apply to St Andrews (UCAS or Common Application)
Two working days later, open the International Undergraduate Scholarships form in My Application
Select the Accommodation Award and give household income details
Submit by 27 January 2027

score_reason: Small top-up, but confirmed and combinable with the tuition scholarship.

about.en:
Funded by the mining company Rio Tinto, this Imperial College London scholarship pays full overseas tuition fees and a stipend of £17,082 a year to three new undergraduates in the Department of Earth Science and Engineering. Eligible degrees are the BSc and MSci in Earth and Planetary Science, Geology and Geophysics (including the year-abroad variants).

It is limited to applicants ordinarily resident in Argentina, Guinea, Madagascar, China, Mongolia or South Africa. You need a conditional or unconditional offer and must complete the scholarship form by 28 May 2027. Selection is on academic achievement and potential and on the application, with decisions after A-level results in August.

en: Full overseas tuition + £17,082 a year
3 awards for geology, geophysics and earth science
Residents of Argentina, Guinea, Madagascar, China, Mongolia, South Africa
